title: Christmas, the child
hookLine: Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus, God come as a child in a stable (Luke 2)

lines: A BABY IN A FEEDING TROUGH.
cards: Trees indoors. Lights along the rooflines. A man in a red suit.
Songs in the shops from November on. Christmas has collected a lot. Peel it away, layer by layer, and what's underneath is small.
A couple far from home, with nowhere proper to stay. A baby, wrapped up tight and laid in an animal's feeding trough. And the first people told about it are shepherds, working the night shift.

teach.b: Luke chapter two. Mary and Joseph travel to Bethlehem for a census.

In the King James words: "And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn." A manger is a feeding trough.
Then an angel appears to shepherds in the fields: "Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people."
Christians call this the incarnation: the belief that God, in Jesus, came into the world not as a king in a palace but as a helpless baby, announced first to laborers. Now the honest part.

teach.h: NO DATE, NO SNOW IN THE TEXT.
teach.b: The Gospels never give a date; December twenty-fifth came later, from the church's calendar, and some Orthodox churches keep Christmas on January seventh because they follow an older calendar.
Luke doesn't mention snow, or cold, or a donkey, or any animals at all; the manger is the only hint of them. The word translated inn may simply mean a guest room in a crowded family house.
The cold in today's line comes from carols and from how people have pictured it for centuries, not from the text.
But the picture has lasted for a reason: a child in the cold is someone you can't ignore. Look back over the week. Two commandments: love your neighbor.
The Beatitudes: blessed are the peacemakers. The Lord's Prayer: daily bread. Grace: given, not earned.
Easter: new life. Paul: love is patient. And the child, whose birth all of it looks back to.

how: Christians celebrate Christmas with services on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, many after the four weeks of Advent; many churches set up a nativity scene and read Luke 2 aloud.

games.q: you're an angel with the biggest news in the world. who do you tell first?
games.why: in Luke 2 the angel appears to shepherds in the fields: good tidings of great joy, to all people.

practice: Picture the scene without the decorations: the trough, the cold night, the shepherds. Then let it move to now: who near you is, in some way, out in the cold?
A new neighbor, a lonely relative, someone sleeping outside; hold them a moment, and let one small gift you could give come to you: a coat, a meal, an hour.
